what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Synthetic users driving a real browser find real problems
sections.para: Five to ten invented users drive a real browser one screenshot at a time, are interviewed, and their findings are ordered by cost. On newsroom.sgit.ai five readers took 62 steps, asked 51 unanswered questions and produced 31 findings, six blocking, and four left. One was a real bug: 51 of 527 figures missing.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Give the agent the screenshot, never the page code
sections.para: A synthetic user is a record of situation, question, knowledge and reasons to leave. Claude Sonnet plays each user in parallel, with the study kept in a repository or vault. Write the expected journey first, interview everyone with the same questions, order findings by cost, and check surprising ones before publishing.

sections.label: What you need
sections.line: Three pieces: Sonnet, a browser helper, a study store
sections.para: Claude Sonnet is good enough to play each user, while Opus writes personas and checks findings. A 58-line Playwright helper takes one action per call and records the browser's own log. The study lives in a public GitHub repository or an encrypted sgit vault shared by a read-key link.

sections.label: The method, step by step
sections.line: Eight steps from choosing users to running again
sections.para: Choose five to ten users including a sceptic and a phone user, write profile records and expected journeys, then drive the browser from screenshots only, capped at 14 actions, against a verified local copy. Interview with ten questions, order findings by cost, check each one, and publish. Newsroom ratings were 2, 2, 3, 3 and 2.

sections.label: What went wrong, so you can skip it
sections.line: Most of the time went on our own mistakes
sections.para: The helper reloaded the page every step, charging the reading meter again, and scrolling stuck; all five runs were redone after fixes. Restoring scroll before images loaded caused two artefact findings. Claude Code's permission mode blocked live-site browsing, so a verified local copy was served and Dinis approved one narrow rule.

sections.label: A template to start from
sections.line: A template prompt and file layout to start from
sections.para: Each persona agent is told it plays one invented user, follows the observe, think, question, act loop, drives the browser only through step.mjs, and decides only from screenshots, at most 14 actions. It writes run.json with steps, interview, a 1 to 5 rating and three to six costed findings.

sections.label: What is next
sections.line: Every site gets five users before it is done
sections.para: Each site will be run with five users, and the same five again after fixes. The newsroom findings go to its session, starting with the 51 missing figures and a plain line at the top. Personas can be shared between sites to turn separate studies into comparisons.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: three published synthetic user study vaults
sections.para: From a voice memo by Dinis Cruz and three studies opened with read keys: store.sgit.ai on 15 September 2026, riskmandate.ai on 16 September and newsroom.sgit.ai on 10 October. Newsroom runs used Chromium against a local copy of v0.6.1, with Claude Sonnet personas and Claude Opus assembling the article.
